Subject: Private hosting — initial feasibility inputs (RFP attached)

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Pinebrook leadership asked us to get a tighter read on what a private hosting engagement would actually look like from a technical and resourcing standpoint before we move to procurement. I attached the RFP we prepared — sections we care most about are: network boundary, telemetry, data residency and encryption at rest/in transit, SLA targets, and upgrade windows.

Top asks from my side:
- High-level runbook: what does an internal pilot look like (1 rack? single-region? minimal oncall?)
- What telemetry/logging we need to capture and which artifacts you can provide (e.g., audit logs, API call traces)
- A first-pass list of Redwood deliverables vs. Pinebrook deliverables for a pilot
- Any blockers for supporting a private VPC + on-prem agent model (firewall ports, NAT, egress patterns)

Can you point me to someone on your side who can map these items into a short impact matrix and an initial resource ask for our procurement review? We are aiming to have internal approvals by end of June.

Attachments: pinebrook_rfp_v2.pdf (PDF)

Thanks,
Erin
Director, Product Integrations
Pinebrook Health

Team — looped in the right folks from Pinebrook. They want a concise impact matrix + staffing ask for procurement by end of June. I sketched a quick set of questions for us to resolve before we share a slide with product/procurement: 

1) API contract & telemetry boundary
   - Do we require any API changes for private installs (mutual TLS, tenant header, heartbeat endpoints)?
   - What level of request/response traces will we persist on the customer side vs. centrally?

2) Operational responsibilities
   - Who owns infra provisioning (Redwood, Pinebrook, or EdgeOps)?
   - Oncall model for the pilot (hand-off to customer ops after N weeks?)

3) Security & compliance
   - KMS/HSM requirements, attestations, and evidence we can hand off in the pilot window

4) Network connectivity
   - Egress patterns, fixed IPs, ports we need opened (need to be specific)

5) Pilot sizing & rollback
   - Minimal pilot: workload profile we recommend (qps, sequence lengths, expected tokens/day)
   - Clear rollback criteria and a maintenance window cadence

Action items: Karthik, please produce a short technical impact matrix (tabular) covering API, infra, and deployment steps. Kimberly, please capture compliance artifacts and minimum requirements for SOC2 evidence and KMS integration. Marcus, please draft a minimal staffing matrix (roles, weeks committed) for a 12-week pilot. I will own the executive summary and scheduling.

I attached a template (redwood-vpc-onprem-impact-matrix.xlsx) and a dry-run checklist. Use these as starting points.

Priya
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Private hosting — initial feasibility inputs (RFP attached)

Thanks — I started a draft matrix (see sheet 'technical-summary' in the attached). High-level notes / open technical questions we should resolve:

- Connectivity: we support two models: outbound-only (customer NAT to our fleet) and VPN/Direct Connect with mutual TLS. For Pinebrook's air-gapped-ish phrasing, we need to confirm if they allow outbound TLS to a set of fixed IPs, or if they require inbound VPNs. Each approach changes operational complexity and oncall posture.

- API surface: no protocol-level changes required for most workloads. For private installs we recommend adding a lightweight heartbeat endpoint and a diagnostic endpoint (read-only) for remote support. If Pinebrook requires mutual TLS client certs, we'll need to extend the onboarding playbook (estimated +2 engineer-weeks).

- KV cache persistence: if they want model warm-start across restarts, we need an NFS/S3-compatible store or redis cluster; that adds stateful infra and backup responsibilities. For pilot we can run without persistence and accept warm-start cold penalty.

- Observability: we can ship local audit logs and a bundle of rotated traces. Remote metrics (aggregated) are optional. Need to confirm retention window and whether Pinebrook wants us to push metrics into their Prometheus/Grafana.

- Upgrade path and orchestration: recommended pilot uses Kubernetes on customer side with our operator to simplify upgrades; if they don't allow k8s we fall back to a managed VM approach which increases ops overhead.

Open asks for Pinebrook (please Erin):
- Do you have a fixed-IP egress block for 3rd-party services?
- Will your network/security team accept TLS to our fixed egress addresses or do they require inbound VPNs?
- Do you need KV persistence between restarts for the pilot?

I'll attach the draft matrix for internal review. If we agree on the outbound-only model with heartbeat endpoint, we estimate: 1 infra engineer (2 wks), 1 platform engineer (3 wks), 0.5 SRE on-call overlap during pilot ramp. If we need mutual TLS + persistent KV the ask increases to ~2 infra + 2 platform + 1 SRE for the pilot.

Karthik
Principal Architect, Redwood Inference

Quick security/compliance checklist notes to include in the matrix:

- KMS: we can support customer-managed keys via KMIP/HSM or cloud KMS depending on where the KMS lives. We need Pinebrook to confirm key lifecycle policy and access controls.
- Audit logs: we will produce signed, timestamped audit bundles (local) and an export option. Clarify retention requirement (30/90/365 days).
- Pen test & vulnerability scans: Pinebrook should provide a scan window. For on-prem we require CVE patch cadence agreement; if they will not patch we charge for managed patching as an add-on.
- Data classification: confirm PHI/PII handling. If PHI is in scope we must run a specific SOC2 + HITRUST gap analysis (adds timeline risk).
- Attestations: we can hand-off SOC2 artifacts for our hosted components. For private installs we provide configuration guidance and checklists but cannot attest to customer-controlled infrastructure compliance.

Open items for procurement slide: list minimal legal clauses they should expect (data custodian responsibilities, incident response SLAs, support window, encryption key ownership). I'll draft language snippets for the procurement team.

Kimberly
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
